items.summary: arXiv:2610.41574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unlike autoregressive (AR) models, diffusion language models (DLMs) permit parallel token updates, flexible generation, and bidirectional attention, but leading systems rely on costly pretraining or full-model fine-tuning. We present Build Your Own DLM (BYOD), a generalizable LoRA-only recipe for parameter-efficient AR-to-DLM conversion. Without architecture-specific tuning, BYOD induces diffusion generation in Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B, and Ministral 8B; to our knowledge, this is the first reported AR-to-DLM conversion of a Mistral model. The adapters comprise 4.1-5.8% of final para…
items.title: BYOD: Build Your Own DLM - Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Model Conversion

items.summary: arXiv:2610.40726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) is becoming a mainstream paradigm for post-training large language models (LLMs), as it improves training efficiency by updating the model as rollouts arrive. Recent work argues that group-wise sampling in GRPO does not naturally fit asynchronous RL training because rollout lengths follow a long-tailed distribution, and proposes Single-rollout Asynchronous Optimization (SAO) to improve stability and off-policy behavior, especially on agentic tasks. However, SAO relies on a closed-source value model obtained from scaling value pretraining. In this paper,…
items.title: Li$^{2}$SAO: Lifting Light Singl-Rollout Asynchronous RL Optimization via Group-Relative Actor-Critic Bootstrapping

items.summary: arXiv:2610.41079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many automated decisions in education involve choosing from a fixed set of options: assigning a rubric score, checking whether an answer meets a marking criterion, or identifying the first wrong step in a solution. Generative language models are increasingly used to make these decisions, but their responses require parsing, longer outputs increase inference costs, and confidence expressed in words does not necessarily reflect the probability of being correct. We present EDU-Jev, a family of single-pass ("System One") decision models at 0.8B, 2B and 4B parameters. Given an assessment context and…
items.title: EDU-Jev Training System-One Decision Models for Education

items.summary: arXiv:2610.41177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents execute tasks through repeated model calls over evolving histories of reasoning, actions, and tool feedback. Aggregate speculative-decoding metrics merge these distinct decisions, providing limited guidance on where draft supervision is needed. We present TraceSpec, a framework connecting trajectory evaluation with adaptive draft training. It combines dynamic execution with fixed-prefix replay and introduces TraceSpec-Traj, a corpus of 10,000 training states and 2,500 test states spanning browsing and software engineering. Analysis of five speculative baselines reveals that aggregate…
items.title: TraceSpec: Understanding and Improving Speculative Decoding for LLM Agents

items.summary: Agentic assistants built on frontier models run a multi-step tool loop, and paying frontier prices on every step is hard to sustain at production scale. This post shows how to use sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD) to transfer a frontier teacher's agentic behavior into a small, lower-cost student on Amazon SageMaker AI.

items.title: Density-Guided Bootstrap Boundaries for Latent World-Model Reinforcement Learning

items.summary: arXiv:2610.41074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Low-precision training reduces computation but introduces additional rounding error. We theoretically study how stochastic rounding (SR) affects prediction risk as model size, training time, and precision change. We consider a two-layer linear network with a fixed random first layer, trained by mini-batch SGD on fresh Gaussian data with power-law spectra. At each SGD step, the features used in forward and backward computations are rounded independently. We prove matched upper and lower bounds on prediction error for the final model and for uniform parameter averaging, with general learning-ra…
items.title: Where, When, and How Many Bits? Scaling Laws for SGD with Stochastic Rounding

items.summary: arXiv:2610.41956v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate forecasting with uncertainty quantification is critical in a variety of scientific applications ranging from epidemiology and economics to energy systems and earth sciences. Yet most forecasting models still need to be developed and trained separately for each domain-specific dataset. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) aim to remove this limitation and enable the application of the same model across domains through large-scale pretraining. However, most existing TSFMs treat each time series independently and therefore cannot model interactions among time series and external driver…
items.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting

items.summary: arXiv:2605.25592v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study optimal experimental design for multinomial logit (MNL) bandits, where an agent repeatedly selects a subset of $K$ items from a ground set of size $N$ and observes single-choice feedback. Unlike linear or generalized linear bandits, MNL bandits have a combinatorial action space, which makes classical optimal design approaches and naive optimization over all subsets computationally intractable. items.title: Optimal Design for Multinomial Logit Model with Applications to Best Assortment Identification
